description: An army travels on its stomach, and this wagon train is designed to keep that stomach full. Composed of five heavy wagons connected via a series of flexible corridors, this caravan carries provisions and provides dining services for troops. The lead and middle wagons contain full-service galleys while the second and fourth wagons are stocked to the brim with foodstuffs. The last wagon in the caravan contains a boiler and scullery services for cleaning kitchen utensils and dishes. On the roof of each wagon is an herb garden to ensure a fresh supply for all meals, and mounted beneath all wagons are water and beer storage. Each cook’s caravan carries enough supplies to feed its crew, passengers, 12 Large creatures, and 500 soldiers for a month before needing to be restocked.

the Speed of the slowest pulling creature (pulled by 12 Large creatures)
This vehicle must move twice its length for each 90-degree turn it makes.

description:
The artistic echo of the Ekujae hero Iyalirrin animates the _Anima Robe’s_ stitching to display embroidered reactions to situations experienced by the wearer. The _Anima Robe’s_ telepathic voice is filled with confidence (almost to the point of cockiness) and is supportive, often encouraging his partner to take risky or showy actions yet never to the extent that would put them in significant harm’s way.

The _Anima Robe_ grants a +3 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks made to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) and to all [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks, and you gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) 15 to [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) damage.
features: +33; precise [low-light vision](/Rules.aspx?ID=2411) and hearing within 30 feet

<actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** The _Anima Robe_ billows as if in a blustery wind and attempts to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390) a creature you’re adjacent to.

<actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** The robe’s hood rises up over your head, casting a 4th-rank [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568) to your specifications.

<actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** The robe’s hem swishes, casting a 7th-rank [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568) to your specifications.

<actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** An image of a creature shows up in the robe’s stitching, then appears to come to life; the robe casts an 8th-rank [_illusory creature_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1567) to your specifications. The robe can use an action to [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) this activation for up to 1 minute.

The _Anima Robe_ grants a +3 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks made to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) and to all [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks, and you gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) 15 to [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) damage.

description:
At the height of the Azlant Empire, there were those who had the wealth and skill to elevate the hobby of terrarium-keeping into a truly breathtaking endeavor. By deploying a clockwork sun into a subterranean cavern, these power-drunk overlords introduced a day-night cycle to chambers that otherwise would never have felt the touch of sunlight. At Azlant’s height, an elite association of powerful spellcasters and aristocrats kept vast underground terrariums outfitted with clockwork suns, competing to see who could create the most astounding “personal world.” Yet not all clockwork suns were the playthings of the rich and bored. The one in En-Gokal served a practical purpose, nurturing farmlands that kept the inmates and staff of the prison fed. Even now, centuries after the cataclysmic events of Earthfall, this clockwork sun continues its relentless crawl across the cavern above Underheaven. 

A clockwork sun is an [elephant](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=413)-sized sphere of polished bronze plates fitted with glowing crystals, all arranged around a heart of grinding gears. An array of magical lenses amplifies the energy shed by a single [aeon stone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3055) set in the center of the artifact, generating light that mimics that of a real sun. A series of short, spider-like legs along one side of the sun grants the artifact lumbering mobility. So long as at least one of these appendages remains in contact with a solid surface, the clockwork sun moves as if gravity were pulling it toward that surface, allowing the sun to move along walls and across ceilings with ease (although a clockwork sun walking on a wall or ceiling immediately falls if it loses contact with this surface).
features: <actions string="" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You program the clockwork sun’s motions and periods of illumination over the course of a 24-hour cycle. The clockwork sun follows this cycle exactly and must return to its starting point at the end of each cycle. If it does so, the act of the cycle automatically winds the clockwork sun, and it repeats the cycle. A clockwork sun that encounters an unexpected barrier can navigate simple blockades by moving around or climbing over them—as such, many users set a clockwork sun’s cycle to take less time than 24 hours, giving the artifact plenty of time to return to its starting spot if it’s forced take detours.

A clockwork sun can be destroyed by mundane means, but its armored frame and high Hit Points make them difficult to damage. A clockwork sun reduced to 0 HP is destroyed and explodes in a blast of shrapnel and fire in a 40-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). Creatures in the area take 10d6 piercing and 10d6 fire damage (DC 43 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save).

---

At the height of the Azlant Empire, there were those who had the wealth and skill to elevate the hobby of terrarium-keeping into a truly breathtaking endeavor. By deploying a clockwork sun into a subterranean cavern, these power-drunk overlords introduced a day-night cycle to chambers that otherwise would never have felt the touch of sunlight. At Azlant’s height, an elite association of powerful spellcasters and aristocrats kept vast underground terrariums outfitted with clockwork suns, competing to see who could create the most astounding “personal world.” Yet not all clockwork suns were the playthings of the rich and bored. The one in En-Gokal served a practical purpose, nurturing farmlands that kept the inmates and staff of the prison fed. Even now, centuries after the cataclysmic events of Earthfall, this clockwork sun continues its relentless crawl across the cavern above Underheaven. 

A clockwork sun is an [elephant](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=413)-sized sphere of polished bronze plates fitted with glowing crystals, all arranged around a heart of grinding gears. An array of magical lenses amplifies the energy shed by a single [aeon stone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3055) set in the center of the artifact, generating light that mimics that of a real sun. A series of short, spider-like legs along one side of the sun grants the artifact lumbering mobility. So long as at least one of these appendages remains in contact with a solid surface, the clockwork sun moves as if gravity were pulling it toward that surface, allowing the sun to move along walls and across ceilings with ease (although a clockwork sun walking on a wall or ceiling immediately falls if it loses contact with this surface). 

**Activate—Set Cycle** <actions string="" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You program the clockwork sun’s motions and periods of illumination over the course of a 24-hour cycle. The clockwork sun follows this cycle exactly and must return to its starting point at the end of each cycle. If it does so, the act of the cycle automatically winds the clockwork sun, and it repeats the cycle. A clockwork sun that encounters an unexpected barrier can navigate simple blockades by moving around or climbing over them—as such, many users set a clockwork sun’s cycle to take less time than 24 hours, giving the artifact plenty of time to return to its starting spot if it’s forced take detours. 

As part of setting the clockwork sun’s cycle, you also determine the periods during which the artifact is illuminated; the total illumination time can’t be longer than half the sun’s total cycle time (typically 12 hours). While illuminated, a clockwork sun sheds bright light equivalent to that of a sunny day to a radius of 1 mile. A sighted creature that ends their turn within 20 feet of an illuminated clockwork sun and didn’t [Avert Gaze](/Actions.aspx?ID=2309) during their turn must succeed at a DC 43 Fortitude save or be [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1 minute ([blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 minute on a critical failure). Creatures at a further distance can look directly at the light without fear, as it’s not as intense as true sunlight. 

Creatures that are vulnerable to sunlight (such as [deros](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=388) or [vampires](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=181)) do not treat the light of a clockwork sun as true sunlight, but if they start their turn within the illumination, they must succeed at a DC 43 Will save or become [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1 (sickened 2 on a critical failure) from the minor but discomforting pain the near sunlight induces.

**Destruction** A clockwork sun can be destroyed by mundane means, but its armored frame and high Hit Points make them difficult to damage. A clockwork sun reduced to 0 HP is destroyed and explodes in a blast of shrapnel and fire in a 40-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). Creatures in the area take 10d6 piercing and 10d6 fire damage (DC 43 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save).

description:
The origins of the notorious _Dullahan Codex_ are shrouded in mystery. Some legends claim it belongs to a [dullahan](/Monsters.aspx?ID=171) whose head was taken by the [Grim Reaper](/Monsters.aspx?ID=250). Others attribute its creation to a powerful necromancer whose name has been lost to time. Whatever the truth, the grimoire has passed down through the ages, sometimes via mortal hands and other times mysteriously appearing among the possessions of its next target. It deserves its reputation for dooming those who possess it to die, but scholars debate whether the codex causes this fate or merely acts as its harbinger.

 The _Dullahan Codex_ is a jet-black tome bearing a single rune embossed on its cover, and it functions as a _[true endless grimoire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=992)_. Inside, scrawled across its parchment pages in a delicate, spidery script, is a lengthy list of names that always appears in a reader's native alphabet. The grimoire isn't sentient, but it selects its owners, quickly passing out of the hands of those it doesn't choose. An intended victim's name appears on the list of names.

 If your name is on the list and you touch the volume or read from its pages, you must attempt a DC 45 Will save.
features: The codex disappears, moving on to a new victim.
The codex fuses to you, and you become [doomed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9).

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 191 2.0 --- The origins of the notorious _Dullahan Codex_ are shrouded in mystery. Some legends claim it belongs to a [dullahan](/Monsters.aspx?ID=171) whose head was taken by the [Grim Reaper](/Monsters.aspx?ID=250). Others attribute its creation to a powerful necromancer whose name has been lost to time. Whatever the truth, the grimoire has passed down through the ages, sometimes via mortal hands and other times mysteriously appearing among the possessions of its next target. It deserves its reputation for dooming those who possess it to die, but scholars debate whether the codex causes this fate or merely acts as its harbinger. The _Dullahan Codex_ is a jet-black tome bearing a single rune embossed on its cover, and it functions as a _[true endless grimoire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=992)_. Inside, scrawled across its parchment pages in a delicate, spidery script, is a lengthy list of names that always appears in a reader's native alphabet. The grimoire isn't sentient, but it selects its owners, quickly passing out of the hands of those it doesn't choose. An intended victim's name appears on the list of names. If your name is on the list and you touch the volume or read from its pages, you must attempt a DC 45 Will save.
**Critical Success** The codex disappears, moving on to a new victim.
**Success** The codex fuses to you.
**Failure** The codex fuses to you, and you become [doomed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9).
**Critical Failure** As failure, but you're doomed 2. If you attempt to get rid of the codex while it's fused to you, it returns to your possession within an hour. Each day the codex is fused to you, you must attempt another Will saving throw, but a critical success does nothing. The doomed value from the codex can decrease only after it's no longer fused to you; once it's fused to you, you remain its intended victim unless you complete a [_freedom_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=11) ritual aimed at ending this 10th-rank effect. (On a critical failure with this ritual, the codex adds all casters to its list.) You can redirect the curse by inscribing another person's name in the grimoire and succeeding at a DC 40 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) check. Doing so is an evil act. If the curse is ritually ended or redirected, or the chosen victim dies, the codex moves on to a new victim.

description: The elixir of rejuvenation restores a creature to full health and eradicates toxins affecting it. When you drink this elixir, you're restored to your maximum Hit Points, and all afflictions of 20th level or lower affecting you are removed.
markdown:
**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 288 1.1 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L **Activate**([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) --- The elixir of rejuvenation restores a creature to full health and eradicates toxins affecting it. When you drink this elixir, you're restored to your maximum Hit Points, and all afflictions of 20th level or lower affecting you are removed.
You can instead administer this elixir to a creature that has been dead for a week or less. When you do, that creature is instantly brought back to life with 1 Hit Point and no spell slots, Focus Points, or other daily resources. Elixirs of life accelerate a living creature's natural healing processes and immune system. While wielding the staff, you gain a +3 circumstance bonus to checks to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about any sort of [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600).

description:
Fashioned from a swath of Mogaru’s red-and-black hide and trimmed with Agyra’s rough scales in green, blue, and white, this cloak draws upon the power of both kaiju, but at considerable cost. Any [kaiju](/Traits.aspx?ID=383) within a 5-mile radius of the Final Scalecloak can sense the presence and nature of the item, and can also determine whether it’s being worn by a mortal. This sense grows stronger as the item and kaiju near one another, until the kaiju can pinpoint exactly where the cloak is and who currently possesses it.

When worn, the Final Scalecloak grants you [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 15 to physical and precision damage, [immunity](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), and a [Fly speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350) of 60 feet. You are unaffected by strong winds while flying.
features: <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320); you gain the effects of a 6th-rank [_telepathy_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1719) spell but can use it only to communicate with Gargantuan [animals](/Traits.aspx?ID=531) and [beasts](/Traits.aspx?ID=547). Most kaiju are [hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=80) toward you for wearing the Final Scalecloak, however, requiring great effort to calm them enough to have a conversation.

<actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320); a nimbus of crackling electricity surrounds you for 1 minute. You gain a +4 status bonus to AC against ranged projectiles that are at least partly made of metal. If a foe attempts to [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) you with an unarmed attack or melee attack with a weapon at least partly made of metal, that creature takes 3d10 [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586) damage ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) DC 40 Reflex save).
The Final Scalecloak is torn to shreds if the wearer is struck by an attack or effect from both Agyra and Mogaru within the same round.

description:
The stoic echo of Candlaron the Sculptor, architect of the aiudara network, infuses the _Guiding Star Orb_. As long as you have him invested, the _Guiding Star Orb_ orbits your body instead of needing to be held in one hand. You can stow the _Guiding Star Orb_ with an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action, and he can be snatched out of the air with a successful [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=2383) action against you. When stowed, the _Guiding Star Orb_ remains invested, but if he’s removed from you via Disarm, your investment ends if you don’t reclaim him by the end of your next turn. The _Guiding Star Orb’s_ voice is scholarly and precise, speaking telepathically with clearly enunciated but often complex words, and he assumes you’re educated enough to keep up with his academic dialogue.

As long as you have the _Guiding Star Orb_ invested, [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) effects created by you or the Guiding Star Orb aren’t affected by the Witchbole’s meddling with teleportation effects, and they can’t be [counteracted](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) by the Witchbole.
features: +33; precise [low-light vision](/Rules.aspx?ID=2411) and hearing within 30 feet

<actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631), [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727))    **Effect** The _Guiding Star Orb_ creates a beam of bright light and fires it at a creature within 30 feet. That creature must attempt a DC 43 Fortitude save, after which that creature is temporarily immune to Blinding Spark for 24 hours.

<actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** By focusing, the _Guiding Star Orb_ embeds your current location within. Thereafter, anyone who touches the _Guiding Star Orb_ while casting a spell with the teleportation trait to travel to this location arrives precisely, without any inaccuracy at all. The _Guiding Star Orb_ can have up to three locations embedded at a time; if this activity is used a fourth time, the new location replaces the oldest stored one.

<actions string="" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** A shimmering magical archway appears next to you as the _Guiding Star Orb_ casts a 9th-rank teleport to your specifications. If you’re teleporting to an aiudara you’ve visited before, you and the targets appear precisely at that location. If you’re teleporting to Lotusgate in Kyonin, this effect functions as [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1576) if you aren’t on the same plane as Kyonin.

Resembling little more than a simple iron pipe with a handle, _Kaldemash's Lament_ is one of the most well-known star guns in all of Arcadia. Legends state the Crowned Regent Kaldemash helped forge one of the first star guns millennia ago. While the star gun served Kaldemash as a powerful weapon, its most notable achievement was the accidental killing of one of Kaldemash's greatest friends. This death is what caused the regent to recognize the true destructive power of the star guns and led to him developing the Star Code, a set of rules of engagement and proper use of firearms still in use in Arcadia today. Although Kaldemash never named the weapon himself, all legends that mention the weapon refer to it as _Kaldemash's Lament_.

 The legendary weapon is a _+3 [major striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [ quickstrike](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2844)_ advanced firearm with a range increment of 90 feet. It deals 4d6 force damage (with the _major striking_ rune included) and has the [concealable](/Traits.aspx?ID=327), [concussive](/Traits.aspx?ID=401), and [fatal d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=178) traits. You don't take a penalty when dealing nonlethal damage with the weapon. Like most star guns, _Kaldemash's Lament_ uses magic to function and doesn't require ammunition or [black powder](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1190).

 If you use _Kaldemash's Lament_ as part of a duel in which all parties are in agreement on the terms, the gun's supernatural instincts help you make the quickest draw. You roll twice and take the higher result on your initiative roll for the duel; this is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect. In addition, you can draw _Kaldemash's Lament_ as a free action at the start of your turn during the duel. If you attempt to fire the star gun in bad faith at a dueling opponent once they have surrendered, been defeated, or the duel is over, _Kaldemash's Lament_ flies out of your hand and you can't pick it up, hold it, or wield it for 10 minutes.

description:
This dried, gnarled hand is clenched in a fist, waiting for a creature to pick it up. When you pick up the _monkey's paw_, the hand opens, revealing three withered fingers. The _monkey's paw_ grants you three wishes (with the effects of a success on the [_wish_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=125) ritual), curling one finger after every one. Once you pick up the _monkey's paw_, you cannot discard the hand until it returns to a clenched fist by granting its three wishes. Any attempts to discard the hand, even with the effects of a _wish_ ritual, are unsuccessful as the _monkey's paw_ reappears among your possessions within 1d4 hours; it doesn't work for any other creature in the intervening time. The hand returns even if another creature steals it from you. Once you make all three wishes, the _monkey's paw_ uses [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1576) to travel to a random point in the multiverse.

 Whenever the _monkey's paw_ hears you utter a statement that sounds like a wish, even if you don't use the words “I wish,” it activates and grants a twisted, horrifying version of your wish, producing any effect within the possibility of _wish_ ritual, and potentially a greater effect at the GM's discretion.

description:
An [alchemist](/Classes.aspx?ID=56) with the [Craft Philosopher's Stone](/Feats.aspx?ID=127) feat adds the formula for this item to their [formula book](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2724). This allows them to create a philosopher's stone once per month during their daily preparations using advanced alchemy. Unlike other items created with advanced alchemy, the philosopher's stone remains potent for 1 month or until the alchemist creates a new one. This is the only way to create a philosopher's stone.

 At a glance, a philosopher's stone appears to be an ordinary, sooty piece of natural rock. Breaking the rock open with a [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=2375) action (DC 35) reveals a cavity at the stone's heart. The cavity is lined with a rare type of quicksilver that can transmute base metals into precious metals or create an elixir of rejuvenation. To use the quicksilver, you must be legendary in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) and have the [Alchemical Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=5117) feat. You can then use the stone's quicksilver for one of two effects.

The heroism of Kyloss Syndar, founder of Greengold and slayer of the demonic hydra Slithermaw, imprinted this suit of armor with a gleaming, prismatic sheen that sparkles under bright light. The telepathic voice of _Slithermaw’s Bane_ is boisterous and grandiose, encouraging his partner to take up leadership roles while also providing advice to maintain loyalty and strengthen bonds of friendship. 

_Slithermaw’s Bane_ is a suit of _[+3 major resilient ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804) [greater fortification](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2789) high-grade [elven chain](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2801)_ that grants his wearer poison [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) 15, and the item bonus his resilient rune grants to saving throws versus poison increases by 1 to +4.
features: +34; precise [low-light vision](/Rules.aspx?ID=2411) and hearing within 30 feet

<actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A creature [grapples](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) you;  **Effect** Poison wells up from the armor’s links to seep into the triggering creature’s body, causing it to suffer wracking pains as if it was being stung by thousands of angry wasps. The triggering creature takes 7d6 [persistent poison damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) (DC 34 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2247) Fortitude save); this persistent damage can’t be ended as long as the triggering creature continues to grapple you. _Slithermaw’s Bane_ can’t activate [Calistria’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=279) Sting using his actions.

<actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** _Slithermaw’s Bane_ attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) a [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578) or [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) [affliction](/Rules.aspx?ID=2389) affecting you, with a counteract rank of 9th and a +25 modifier to the roll (+30 modifier if the source of the disease or poison effect on you was created by a [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600)).

<actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You alter the exterior of the armor to better adapt to the surrounding [terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2365): [aquatic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2770), [arctic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2773), [desert](/Rules.aspx?ID=2776), [forest](/Rules.aspx?ID=2779), [mountain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2783), [plains](/Rules.aspx?ID=2789), sky, [swamp](/Rules.aspx?ID=2792), or [underground](/Rules.aspx?ID=2808). You [ignore difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2367) within the chosen [environment](/Rules.aspx?ID=590) and gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against [environmental hazards](/Rules.aspx?ID=2588), [natural disasters](/Rules.aspx?ID=2823), and extreme temperatures that originate from that terrain. You’re also protected from [severe and extreme heat or severe and extreme cold](/Rules.aspx?ID=2820) (your choice when you activate this ability). This effect lasts until your next daily preparations or the next time you activate it, whichever comes first.

**Activate—Adaptation** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You alter the exterior of the armor to better adapt to the surrounding [terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2365): [aquatic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2770), [arctic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2773), [desert](/Rules.aspx?ID=2776), [forest](/Rules.aspx?ID=2779), [mountain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2783), [plains](/Rules.aspx?ID=2789), sky, [swamp](/Rules.aspx?ID=2792), or [underground](/Rules.aspx?ID=2808). You [ignore difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2367) within the chosen [environment](/Rules.aspx?ID=590) and gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against [environmental hazards](/Rules.aspx?ID=2588), [natural disasters](/Rules.aspx?ID=2823), and extreme temperatures that originate from that terrain. You’re also protected from [severe and extreme heat or severe and extreme cold](/Rules.aspx?ID=2820) (your choice when you activate this ability). description:
The echo of the snowcaster Jelarial causes _Wintershot_ to become chill to the touch, yet despite feeling as cold as ice, she never causes harm or discomfort to her partner. Wintershot’s string issues a soft hissing sound, as of snow softly falling, and snowflakes drift down from the string and swiftly melt each time the bow is fired. _Wintershot’s_ voice is eager and excitable, often waxing poetic on a nearby object or creature of beauty or offering compliments to her partner.

_Wintershot_ is a _[+3 major striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [greater frost ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2839) [holy ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2842) [composite shortbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=435)_. When making a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with _Wintershot_, targets don’t gain [concealment](/Rules.aspx?ID=424) from the effects of mist or [precipitation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2816), and circumstance penalties to attacks imparted from strong winds are negated.
features: +35; precise [low-light vision](/Rules.aspx?ID=2411) and hearing within 30 feet

<actions string="Single Action" /> ([cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** _Wintershot_ can’t use this activation. When you activate Auroral Shine, fire an arrow at a target. If you hit, instead of dealing damage with the arrow, the creature struck must attempt a DC 43 Fortitude save.

The creature is surrounded by shimmering lights akin to the aurora, causing it to become dazzled for 2 rounds. If the creature was [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83), it becomes [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) instead. If the creature was already concealed for any other reason, it’s no longer concealed.
As success, but the creature also takes 6d6 [persistent cold damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), and the lights affect the creature for 1 minute.
As success, but the creature also takes 6d6 persistent cold damage, and the lights affect the creature for 10 minutes.

<actions string="Single Action" /> ([light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** _Wintershot_ fires an arrow-shaped construct of ice straight upward. The arrow soars to a height of 500 feet, or until it strikes a solid surface like a ceiling. When it reaches its apex, it explodes in a brilliant burst, creating a 100-foot radius area of [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) in the next 100 feet. In the night sky, this beacon can be seen clearly for miles. The beacon remains lit for up to 1 minute in a color of _Wintershot’s_ choice. Alternatively, _Wintershot_ can fire this Signal Flare like a normal arrow to attempt to [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) a target her partner can see—if it hits, the arrow inflicts normal damage and attempts to counteract one darkness effect of Wintershot’s choice that affects the creature struck, with a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) rank of 9th and a +25 modifier to the roll (+30 modifier if the source of the [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=569) effect was created by a [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600)).

<actions string="Two Actions" /> ([cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631))    **Effect** _Wintershot_ causes the deep chill of winter to settle upon a single creature she can see or hear within 30 feet. That creature must attempt a DC 43 Fortitude save, after which point they’re temporarily immune to Rimecrust for 24 hours.

The creature’s discomfort and shivering from the sudden drop in temperature causes it to become [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of its next turn. Creatures that are [immune](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to cold are immune to this effect.

The creature becomes encrusted with ice. It becomes [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 and [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) for 1 minute, or until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) from the crusting ice (DC 43).

The creature is slowed 1 and [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) by crusting ice until it Escapes (DC 43). After it Escapes, it remains slowed 1 and [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) for 1 minute from the lingering cold.

The creature remembers your existence but no details about you or your interactions. For example, they remember speaking with an individual of your most basic biological traits, such as a human woman, but not your name, appearance, or other specific features.

features: <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** _Graymist_ manifests a dangerous-looking assassin, who appears to step out out of hiding at any point you can sense within 60 feet. This allows _Graymist_ to [Create a Diversion](/Actions.aspx?ID=2387) using his [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) skill, but the closest creature to where the Diverting Reveal appears must attempt a DC 44 Will save or become so startled by the assassin’s sudden appearance that they become [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 3 (or stunned 6 on a critical failure). description: Carved from a scale of the [kaiju](/Traits.aspx?ID=383) Igroon, this jagged shield refracts light around it in a shimmering haze. A _scale of Igroon_ (Hardness 20, HP 160, BT 80) recovers 4 Hit Points at the start of its wielder's turn. When you [Raise a Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=98), you can use the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) reaction with the scale of Igroon to block an attack or effect that deals acid, cold, electricity, fire, force, or sonic damage as well as physical damage.
features: <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** You're in an area of [bright](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) or [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408); **Effect** You angle the shield to refract light. Until the start of your next turn, you gain a +4 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) and [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) and can do so while [observed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=27). This bonus ends if you Activate another ability or use the Shield Block reaction.

<actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** You're in an area of bright light; **Effect** You angle the shield at a target within 60 feet, reflecting light into its eyes. It must attempt a DC 42 Fortitude save.
The target is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) until its next turn begins.
The target is blinded for 1 minute.
The target is blinded for 2d4 hours.

<actions string="Free Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))  **Trigger** You use Shield Block and prevent yourself from taking energy damage from a line, ray, or a direct attack, including a [_force barrage_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1536) spell;  **Effect** You reflect the energy along a trajectory you choose. The effect travels only up to its remaining range, using its original parameters if it strikes other targets.
If a deity, kaiju, spawn of a deity, titan, or being of similar power stomps on a _scale of Igroon_ while in absolute darkness, the shield is destroyed permanently.

description:
The legendary blade _Serithtial_ is said to have been forged by [Iomedae](/Deities.aspx?ID=9), goddess of honor, justice, and valor. She is an intelligent _+4 [major striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [holy](/Equipment.aspx?ID=299) [bastard sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=15)_. Although the sword is made of steel, Serithtial is also treated as [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375) and [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=379), allowing her to deal more damage to certain supernatural creatures. She glows as bright as a [torch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=60), but you or _Serithtial_ can suppress or resume this glow as a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait. In addition, Strikes with _Serithtial_ deal an additional 2d6 damage against creatures that are worshippers of [Zon-Kuthon](/Deities.aspx?ID=20). While wielding _Serithtial_, against effects created by followers of Zon-Kuthon you gain the benefit of [_unfettered movement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1732), a +4 status bonus to saves against [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) and [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) effects, void resistance 10, and suppress the [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9) condition.

 _Serithtial_ was forged as a bastard sword, and she reverts to this shape when no one wields her, but she can also detect what sort of blade her current wielder prefers and transform into it (choosing from [dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3), [shortsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=43), [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=31), [scimitar](/Weapons.aspx?ID=38), [falchion](/Weapons.aspx?ID=18), [greatsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=24), [rapier](/Weapons.aspx?ID=36), or bastard sword) using an action, which she does when first held. The wielder can empathically tell Serithtial to transform at any time by using a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait, after which Serithtial uses an action to transform.

 Serithtial is willing to work with almost any partner as long as they are dedicated to defeating the great wyrm Kazavon and the forces of Zon-Kuthon. If you ignore those threats and pursue your own agenda instead, before long _Serithtial_ attempts to seize control of your body (DC 45 Will save to resist her control), though she typically remains in control for only long enough to find a more worthy partner. You can attempt a new Will save each day to retake control of your body.
features: +28; normal vision and hearing within 60 feet

<actions string="" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** _Serithtial_ spends the appropriate number of actions and casts a 9th-rank [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=148) or [_ring of truth_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1656) spell (DC 45 for either of the two spells).
If Kazavon or a great wyrm shadow dragon who is a worshipper of Zon-Kuthon uses its dragon breath on _Serithtial_ while she is unattended, the sword melts into a pool of mundane iron.

 _Serithtial_ was forged as a bastard sword, and she reverts to this shape when no one wields her, but she can also detect what sort of blade her current wielder prefers and transform into it (choosing from [dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3), [shortsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=43), [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=31), [scimitar](/Weapons.aspx?ID=38), [falchion](/Weapons.aspx?ID=18), [greatsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=24), [rapier](/Weapons.aspx?ID=36), or bastard sword) using an action, which she does when first held. The wielder can empathically tell Serithtial to transform at any time by using a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait, after which Serithtial uses an action to transform.

 Serithtial is willing to work with almost any partner as long as they are dedicated to defeating the great wyrm Kazavon and the forces of Zon-Kuthon. If you ignore those threats and pursue your own agenda instead, before long _Serithtial_ attempts to seize control of your body (DC 45 Will save to resist her control), though she typically remains in control for only long enough to find a more worthy partner. You can attempt a new Will save each day to retake control of your body.

**Activate—Grace of the Inheritor** <actions string="" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** _Serithtial_ spends the appropriate number of actions and casts a 9th-rank [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=148) or [_ring of truth_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1656) spell (DC 45 for either of the two spells).

**Destruction** If Kazavon or a great wyrm shadow dragon who is a worshipper of Zon-Kuthon uses its dragon breath on _Serithtial_ while she is unattended, the sword melts into a pool of mundane iron.

Braided tassels of horsehair dangle from its sturdy haft, and archaic runes in Nidalese script shimmer along the weapon in the presence of shadow magic.

_Shadowpiercer_ ignores [immunity](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) and [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) to precision damage of creatures with the [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) or [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=693) trait, and deals an additional 2d6 precision damage to such creatures. While wielding _Shadowpiercer_, you gain a +2 status bonus to saving throws against [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=569) and shadow effects; this bonus also applies to allies within 60 feet of you while you wield the spear.

If you are a worshipper of [Zon-Kuthon](/Deities.aspx?ID=296), you are [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 4 and [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 4 while carrying or wielding _Shadowpiercer_. If you use a darkness or shadow effect while carrying or wielding _Shadowpiercer_, you become enfeebled 4; this condition’s value reduces by 1 at the start of each day you do not have physical contact with _Shadowpiercer_.
features: <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You touch _Shadowpiercer_ to a [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=569) or [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=693) effect to siphon its energy and bolster yourself. You gain a number of temporary Hit Points equal to four times the effect’s [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) rank. These temporary Hit Points last for 1 hour. In addition, if the effect is causing darkness, that darkness is automatically counteracted within 15 feet of you for as long as you have those temporary Hit Points. This doesn’t provide light—it merely restores the area to its natural illumination level.

<actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Frequency** You don’t currently have the [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) condition; **Trigger** You or an ally within 60 feet is targeted by a [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=569) or [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=693) effect;  **Effect** Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320); the spear drains your vitality to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) the effect. You can attempt to counteract the effect (+46 modifier level, counteract rank 10). You can activate this effect without having a Mythic Point available but doing so makes you [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 2.

_Shadowpiercer_ simply disappears if a worshipper of [Zon-Kuthon](/Deities.aspx?ID=296) casts a 10th-rank [_darkness_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1480) spell on it once a day for an entire month while it is unattended.

description:
Legends claim that some long-forgotten god stole the original bundle of _shots of the First Vault_ from [Abadar's](/Deities.aspx?ID=1) repository. Since then, individual pieces have turned up throughout the multiverse. When you pick up a _shot of the First Vault_, it immediately reshapes itself to function with any ranged weapon and establishes you as its owner until another creature picks it up. As its owner, you can use the shot's single-action activation after shooting it.

 Instead of rolling weapon damage dice, a _shot of the First Vault_ deals 25 damage plus any bonuses or additional damage as if 25 were the result of the weapon's damage dice; the damage type matches that normally dealt by the weapon. Upon damaging a creature, the _shot of the First Vault_ shatters, and the fragments ricochet to hit any other enemies within 30 feet, making attack rolls with the same attack bonus. The shattered fragments remain lodged in the creatures they damage; the creatures are [clumsy 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) while the fragments remain in place. A total of 3 Interact actions are required to remove the fragments from yourself or an adjacent creature; alternatively, a single action and a successful DC 30 [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) check can be used. A critical failure on this Medicine check deals 10 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) to the creature with the embedded fragment.
features: <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32))   **Requirements** The shot is loaded in your ranged weapon, or at hand if your ranged weapon has a reload of 0; **Effect** You recall the _shot of the First Vault_, which automatically reloads itself into your weapon. If the shot had fragmented, the fragments violently dislodge themselves, dealing 15 persistent bleed damage to each creature in which they were embedded. The fragments then unite to re-form the _shot of the First Vault_, which automatically reloads itself into your weapon.

<actions string="Three Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))    **Effect** You line up a perfectly aimed attack directly toward the First Vault. You Strike a creature, then the _shot of the First Vault_ attempts to bring your target with it as it returns to the First Vault. Unless your attack roll is a critical failure, the creature must attempt a DC 45 Reflex save; this effect has the [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93) trait. Regardless, the _shot of the First Vault_ returns to the First Vault.
The creature is [moved](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 1d20x50 feet in the direction you fired. If this causes it to hit a solid object, it takes 50 bludgeoning damage.
The creature is transported to a random location on the plane of [Axis](/Planes.aspx?ID=14).
The creature is transported to the First Vault. Unless it is capable of eluding Abadar's precautions, it is likely unable to escape the Vault on its own.

If 10 _shots of the First Vault_ are all fired at the same group of [keketar](/Monsters.aspx?ID=338) or [izfiitar](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1020) proteans within 1 minute of each other, each shot was a hit, and the shots are then recalled, the shots collide as they attempt to re-form and crumble to dust.

description:
This traditional barrel drum has tacked heads in the old military style of Hwanggot and is painted with a many-colored imperial dragon twined around white and pink lotuses, a symbol of long memory. The dragon holds a scroll in its two front claws that bears the inscription “So that the memory of war may be truthfully recalled.” 

A creature who activates the drum is bound to join its army after death. Once their spirit has fought in a hundred and one battles, they are freed to face whatever fate their soul has earned. However, until this duty is discharged, the dead creature cannot be resurrected, nor can their soul be captured by any other means.
features: <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [incarnate](/Traits.aspx?ID=786), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once every 20 years;   **Effect** Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320); beating the drum summons a spectral army to an area you designate within 500 feet. The army takes its Arrive action when you finish playing. At the end of your next turn, the army [Strides](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) up to 60 feet and then takes its Depart action. The Dragon-Lotus Army follows your orders and attempts to not harm you and your allies when possible. The spectral force isn’t fully a creature. It can’t take any other actions, nor can it be targeted or harmed by [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306), spells, or other effects unless they would be able to target or end a spell effect (such as [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493)). The army is Gargantuan, but it doesn’t block movement.

([emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697)) _The Sound of Thunder_ The beating of the drum amplifies to become like the stomping of hundreds of booted feet. The Dragon-Lotus Army appears in perfect formation and gives a brief, staccato battle cry. All enemies in a 60-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) around the army take 16d10 sonic damage ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) DC 48 Fortitude save); each creature who fails its save is also [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 3 (frightened 4 on a critical failure).

_Devastating Charge_ The army readies their motley collection of weapons and Strides forward up to 100 feet in a straight [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388). Each creature it moves through takes 20d8 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (whichever would be most harmful at the GM’s discretion) with a basic DC 48 Reflex save. A creature who critically fails its save is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).

If the Dragon-Lotus Drum is captured by an enemy of Hwanggot (such as a warring rival nation) and then played continually for 1 week while singing anthems that disparage Hwanggot and its leaders, the drum falls to pieces and the souls bound to it are obliterated.

description:
This rune was created by [Torag](/Deities.aspx?ID=18), god of the forge, protection,  and strategy, and shared with his greatest artisans and warriors. Torag designed a small number of these seals as gifts to allied deities; each one is nearly identical but has a different spell effect when using the reaction activation; for instance, [Sarenrae's](/Deities.aspx?ID=16) seal casts [_sunburst_](/Spells.aspx?ID=326) instead of [_earthquake_](/Spells.aspx?ID=95).

 A seal constantly rings with the quiet sound of a hammer striking an anvil when etched onto a runestone. A _Forgefather's seal_ can be etched only onto armor that can bear two or more property runes, and it is so powerful that it takes the place of two property runes. While wearing armor etched with a _Forgefather's seal_, you gain fire resistance 40. You ignore the armor's check penalty and Speed penalty (if any); if the armor is light or medium, increase its item bonus to AC by 1. In addition, any shield you wield automatically recovers 10 Hit Points at the start of your turn each round.
features: <actions string="Reaction" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You are hit by an attack;  **Effect** The _Forgefather's seal_ glows and your armor shakes as it absorbs the blow. The attack's damage is reduced by 100 and you cast [_earthquake_](/Spells.aspx?ID=95) (DC 40), centered directly on the triggering creature. You decide the area of the earthquake when you Cast the Spell, from as small as the size of the creature and up to a 60-foot burst.

<actions string="Three Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You call upon on the restorative powers of the seal to repair an item within reach. The rune instantly restores the item to full Hit Points, even if the item was destroyed, using the effects of the [_remake_](/Spells.aspx?ID=249) spell, so long as the majority of the item is available for the repair. The seal can restore even magic items and artifacts of its level or lower. Once you have used this ability, the seal's ability to automatically repair shields becomes inactive until the next time you make your daily preparations.

<actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32))  **Trigger** You have not acted yet on your turn;  **Effect** You call upon Torag to defend your allies and those around you, sacrificing yourself in the process. Creatures of your choosing within 60 feet recover all their Hit Points. If any of the creatures are dead, they are instead brought back to life with half of their maximum Hit Points. The chosen creatures also gain a +4 status bonus to AC and saving throws, and [fast healing 15](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=15) for 1 hour. You can use this ability to bring back to life a creature that requires a [_wish_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=125) ritual or divine intervention to raise from the dead, as long as you choose no other creatures within 60 feet to recover. Once you use this activation, you are turned into a perfect statue made from stone or metal that depicts you in a glorious pose honoring your sacrifice, and you can never be restored. The _Forgefather's seal_ remains on this statue and can be transferred to another suit of armor or a runestone as normal.

Using the _Forgefather's seal_ ability to bring the dead back to life on an evil demigod causes it to shatter in a violent explosion that destroys the seal and the statue made as part of the sacrifice, erasing all knowledge of the user from existence. It does, however, bring the demigod back to life.

description: The swirling folds of a _starfaring cloak_ appear to contain the night sky, with the stars rotating hypnotically through its firmament shedding dim light to a range of 10 feet. While wearing the cloak, you gain a +10-foot item bonus to your Speed and a fly Speed equal to your Speed. You can survive comfortably without breathing, in the void of space, and in [severe or extreme cold or heat](/Rules.aspx?ID=642). Also, you gain sustenance from starlight and sunlight, so if you're outdoors for an hour or more per day, you don't need to eat or drink. While wearing the cloak, you can navigate perfectly and unerringly by looking up at the sky.
features: <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) ,[fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You make an attack roll, skill check, or saving throw;  **Effect** Reroll the triggering roll and take the higher result. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect.

<actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The cloak casts [_sleep_](/Spells.aspx?ID=288) at 4th rank (DC 42).

<actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** The cloak casts [_teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=338) at 10th rank. If you name no destination, it teleports you to a random planet in a random location that's safe for you.

If the wearer of a _starfaring cloak_ is bound by [imprisonment](/Rituals.aspx?ID=13) for a century and a day, the cloak dissolves into light. This time is reduced to a year and a day if the wearer is placed in eternal slumber by _imprisonment_ and subjected to the [_nightmare_](/Spells.aspx?ID=208) spell once per day.

features: <actions string="Reaction" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))  **Trigger** You are targeted or included in the area of a fear effect;  **Effect** Calmly swigging a drink on the battlefield turns your foe's attempt to frighten you against them. description:
The silvery glass of this oval mirror displays alluring sights. Its dark wooden frame is studded with small green gems and is carved with a pair of sensuous humanoid shapes—one on the edge of each side of the glass.

 The _Mirror of Sorshen_ can form a bond with a spellcaster who has legendary proficiency in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), who becomes the mirror's owner. Regardless of where the mirror is, as long as the bond remains, the owner is aware of everything the mirror is currently reflecting and can use the mirror's activations.

 Whenever an intelligent creature looks in the mirror, they see an image of a person, creature, or item they find powerfully enticing in some way. The specific image varies depending on the observer, even when more than one creature is looking into the mirror at the same time. Observers are [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=14) by the images in the mirror unless they succeed at a DC 35 Will save each round. On a failure, they stare blankly at the mirror for as long as it remains in view, and if it leaves their view, they stare toward the last place they saw the mirror for several minutes thereafter. This is an [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), and [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) effect. Creatures that are fascinated by the mirror are so deeply entranced that they don't end their fascinated condition automatically even if a creature uses [hostile actions](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) against them or their allies; instead, they can attempt a DC 30 Will save to end the fascination. At the GM's discretion, a truly innocent creature or a creature that has renounced all worldly pleasures might be immune to the mirror's fascination.
features: <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163))    **Effect** You force a creature looking at the mirror to attempt an additional Will save against the mirror's fascination effect, even if they succeeded at their save.

<actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163))   **Requirements** The target must be fascinated by the mirror; **Effect** You control the target for 30 days, with the effect of a critically failed saving throw against [_dominate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=87). If the victim sees the mirror again at any point before this duration expires, the control extends for an additional 30 days from the moment it looked at the mirror again. While there is no initial saving throw, the DC to break free due to commands against the creature's nature is 35.
The _Mirror of Sorshen_ shatters into a thousand pieces if an intelligent but completely innocent creature resists the mirror's attraction and then accidentally drops it.

description: This bizarre machine is a complex arrangement of flasks, tubes, and other alchemical equipment. The _philosopher's extractor_ is designed to create the ultimate alchemical concoctions. The extractor functions as an [exceptional alchemist's toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2702), granting a +4 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks related to alchemy.  When using the extractor to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) an alchemical item or with [infused reagents](/Classes.aspx?ID=1) as part of your daily preparations, you can create impeccable alchemical items. An impeccable alchemical item always uses the maximum numerical value possible for any rolls it requires, such as dealing maximum damage with [alchemist's fire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=75) or restoring the maximum number of Hit Points with an [elixir of life](/Equipment.aspx?ID=91). If the impeccable item has a duration, it lasts twice as long as normal. Finally, an impeccable alchemical item never has a drawback.
features: <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You use the extractor to produce an alchemical item of your level or lower whose formula you know. The extractor can create 56 levels' worth of items per day in this way. For example, the extractor could create two true elixirs of life (19th level) and two moderate elixirs of life (9th level), or eight [comprehension elixirs](/Equipment.aspx?ID=88) (7th level), and so on.

<actions string="" /> 1 hour (manipulate)    **Effect** You take a sizable portion of a creature (at least two-thirds of its original mass) and filter it through the mechanisms of the extractor. After the end of the process, the _philosopher's extractor_ creates a transmogrifying mutagen that imparts the essence of the creature to the drinker. The extractor can make several transmogrifying mutagens simultaneously using the same activation if enough mass is provided at once, up to a maximum of 10 concurrent mutagens. Drinking a transmogrifying mutagen imparts you with one of the creature's unique abilities for 1 hour. This could grant one of several abilities such as a dragon's breath, [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), flight, [frightful presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=17), or immunity to [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145). The ability functions as it did for the original creature, except it uses your class DC or your spell DC (whichever is higher) instead of the creature's DC. The mutagen grants only abilities based on a creature's physiology and never grants magic-related abilities such as innate spells or spellcasting ability. The GM ultimately decides what ability a transmogrifying mutagen grants.

Simultaneously feeding the _philosopher's extractor_ sizable portions of an [aeon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=2), [angel](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=3), [archon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=9), [azata](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=10), [daemon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=26), [demon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=28), [devil](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=30), [protean](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=82), and [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83), each of at least 14th level, along with a [philosopher's stone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=133) causes the device to jam, overheat, and explode. Creatures within 60 feet of the explosion must succeed at a DC 55 Reflex save or become covered in an alchemical slurry that transforms them into a horrifying amalgam of at least two of the creatures used to destroy the machine.

 Unlike normal for [mutagens](/Traits.aspx?ID=116) and [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127) effects, you can drink multiple transmogrifying mutagens and gain benefits from each. When you drink transmogrifying mutagens made from different creatures, you receive abilities from each creature. When you drink multiple transmogrifying mutagens made from the same type of creature, such as multiple mutagens made from trolls, you gain an additional ability for each transmogrifying mutagen you drink, and the duration of the abilities from that creature type increases by 1 hour for each additional concoction you drink.

 However, these additional benefits come with a risk; if you drink a transmogrifying mutagen while at least one other is active, after drinking it, you must succeed at a flat check with a DC equal to the total number of active transmogrifying mutagens you've consumed. On a failure, you fully transform into a member of the species of the latest transmogrifying mutagen you drank, and you almost always go berserk from your change. The transformation may leave some amount of your personality and memories intact, at the GM's discretion.

**Destruction** Simultaneously feeding the _philosopher's extractor_ sizable portions of an [aeon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=2), [angel](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=3), [archon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=9), [azata](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=10), [daemon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=26), [demon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=28), [devil](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=30), [protean](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=82), and [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83), each of at least 14th level, along with a [philosopher's stone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=133) causes the device to jam, overheat, and explode. Creatures within 60 feet of the explosion must succeed at a DC 55 Reflex save or become covered in an alchemical slurry that transforms them into a horrifying amalgam of at least two of the creatures used to destroy the machine.

Stories claim that even metaphorical and abstract concepts, including “a [graveknight’s](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=423) mercy” and “the tears of a [living wildfire](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2982)” have been hammered into solid shape upon _Worldforge_, though the tales disagree about what form those objects took.

The cost of using _Worldforge_, however, is prohibitive for mere mortals. In addition to the fuel and metal it consumes, _Worldforge_ draws upon the user’s physical and spiritual strength to sustain the act of creation. The demand of its magic is such that no one save gods, or those who are nearly gods, can use it and survive.

Mounted upon a base of iron, inscribed with innumerable runes, this immense anvil can be used to forge nearly anything into reality. Stories claim that even metaphorical and abstract concepts, including “a [graveknight’s](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=423) mercy” and “the tears of a [living wildfire](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2982)” have been hammered into solid shape upon _Worldforge_, though the tales disagree about what form those objects took.

The cost of using _Worldforge_, however, is prohibitive for mere mortals. In addition to the fuel and metal it consumes, _Worldforge_ draws upon the user’s physical and spiritual strength to sustain the act of creation. The demand of its magic is such that no one save gods, or those who are nearly gods, can use it and survive.

**Activate—Wondrous Forge** <actions string="" /> ([downtime](/Traits.aspx?ID=580), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** You have the ability to make a [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) check at mythic proficiency (such as that granted by the Artisan’s Calling); **Effect** After spending 2 days setting up the work (or 1 if you have the desired item’s formula) and supplying _Worldforge_ with adequate raw materials (as determined by the GM), you attempt to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=2385) something upon it. The DC and final cost of the item is also determined by the GM. For each day you spend Crafting, you must expend a Mythic Point or your [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) condition increases by 1; this condition can’t be reduced until you have finished Crafting the item or you abandon the project. Each day spent Crafting upon the Worldforge counts as 10 days of normal Crafting time.

If the value of your drained condition reaches 4, you must attempt a DC 46 Fortitude save or [die](/Rules.aspx?ID=2329). If you fail this save or if you abandon the activity, what remains of your project shatters irrecoverably into a multitude of useless fragments.

**Destruction** _Worldforge_ can’t be destroyed as long as [Torag](/Deities.aspx?ID=294) maintains his divinity.

description: This _+4 [major striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [greater brilliant](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1043) [keen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=300) [glaive](/Weapons.aspx?ID=20)_ binds the souls of powerful creatures it slays. The soul can't be returned to life by any means while imprisoned within the glaive and can be freed only by a deed of great benevolence or selflessness. While using the glaive as a weapon, whenever you reduce a sapient creature of 18th level or higher to 0 Hit Points or roll a critical success with a Strike against such a target, the creature must attempt a DC 50 Fortitude save.
features: The glaive siphons the creature's essence, rendering it [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10). If the creature dies from the Strike or while drained in this way, the creature's soul is bound in the glaive.

<actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))  **Trigger** You Strike with the _Whisperer of Souls_;  **Effect** You choose whether the Strike deals lethal or [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188) damage. If the glaive has a reason for doing so, such as slaying a creature whose soul the glaive can absorb, it can defy your choice if you fail a DC 50 Will save.

<actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))  **Trigger** You attempt an [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) check to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=22), [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=24), [Learn a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=25), or [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26);  **Effect** You listen to eldritch secrets the weapon whispers, gaining a +4 item bonus to the triggering check.

<actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** Attempt an Occultism check as if you cast the [legend lore](/Rituals.aspx?ID=15) ritual about a subject. If you roll a success or critical success, you can repeat what the _Whisperer of Souls_ relates to you about the subject. On a critical failure, you and the glaive are drawn into a murmuring void of cold, where your mind is assaulted by strange visions for an entire week. At the end of this time, you reappear and must attempt a DC 50 Will save.
When you return, you can retrain one of your skills into a [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skill about evil creatures or places, as if you had spent 1 week retraining.
As success, but you are [stupefied 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) for 1 week.

As success, but you become [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521). If you were [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517), you instead lose that trait. You must retrain one of your skills into a Lore about unholy creatures or places. You become obsessed with increasing your forbidden knowledge, turning to wicked forces that offer such secrets and compromising your morals further if you must.
